note: The map from a company's SIC code to the sector series its abnormal return is measured against. docs/INPUT_SPEC.md section 4 asks for it by name and says where it lives: the map is data in src/, versioned with the rules, and its default is one exchange-traded fund per SIC division so that the market table computes from the first run. docs/rules.md versions it with the rules rather than with the code, because the sector a company is measured against changes what its abnormal return means.
the_default_is_coarse_on_purpose: One fund per division is the whole of division D, manufacturing, under a single industrials fund -- which is where eleven of the twelve companies in this study land. Narrowing the map to SIC major groups is on the needs-judgment list in docs/next_cycle_tasks.md as a modelling choice no test can settle, and it is an improvement rather than a precondition. Nothing here is narrowed ahead of that decision.
divisions_are_the_standard_ones: The eleven divisions and their code ranges are the Standard Industrial Classification's own, as the classification publishes them; they are not this project's grouping. The ranges do not tile the whole four-digit space -- 1800 to 1999, 6800 to 6999, 9000 to 9099 and 9730 to 9899 are unassigned -- and a code that falls in a gap is refused by name rather than mapped to a neighbour.

broad_market_series.note: The broad-market series every abnormal return is measured against, named here rather than in the code because it moves with the rules for the same reason the sector map does.

divisions.title: Agriculture, Forestry and Fishing
divisions.why: Consumer staples is the listed sector that carries farming, forestry and fishing output.

divisions.title: Mining
divisions.why: The division is led by oil and gas extraction, which is the energy sector.

divisions.title: Construction
divisions.why: Engineering and construction sit in industrials.

divisions.title: Manufacturing
divisions.why: Industrials is the single listed sector that spans a division running from food through chemicals to electronics. This is the coarsest entry in the map and the one the needs-judgment item is about.

divisions.title: Transportation, Communications, Electric, Gas and Sanitary Services
divisions.why: Utilities carries the electric, gas and sanitary services that end the division.

divisions.title: Wholesale Trade
divisions.why: Consumer discretionary is where distribution of goods is listed.

divisions.title: Retail Trade
divisions.why: Consumer discretionary again; retail is its largest constituent.

divisions.title: Finance, Insurance and Real Estate
divisions.why: The financial sector fund covers the whole division.

divisions.title: Services
divisions.why: Prepackaged software and data processing sit at the head of this division, and technology is the listed sector that carries them.

divisions.title: Public Administration
divisions.why: No listed sector fund tracks public administration; industrials is the nearest, and a filer in this division would be unusual enough to reread the map.

divisions.title: Nonclassifiable Establishments
divisions.why: A company the classification declines to place is measured against the broad market rather than against a sector chosen for it.
